transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. I came in because... well, I just can’t make myself go near the front windows at work anymore, or even that part of the street. I keep finding excuses to stay in the back room, even though being out front is a big part of my job. I just can't do it right now.
When you are in those areas, are you worried that if you were to have a panic attack or feel overwhelmed, it would be difficult or embarrassing to leave or get help?

No, that's not really it. I'm not worried about having a panic attack or being embarrassed, or... or not being able to get help. It's just that specific area. I just really don't want to be near those windows or looking out at that part of the street. It doesn't have anything to do with feeling trapped or what other people might think.
Is there something specific that you see when you look out those windows that makes you want to stay away?

No, it's not... it's not really a specific thing I see out there, like a person or a car or anything like that. It's just... the windows themselves, and that part of the street. I don't know, I just can't be near them right now.
Are you afraid that you might fall out of the windows or lose your balance if you get too close to them?
No, it's nothing like that. I'm not afraid of falling or heights or anything. The windows don't even open, anyway. It's just... I just don't want to be near them.
Does the feeling of unease happen only when you are in close proximity to the glass of the windows, or does it persist as long as you are in that specific part of the building?

I'm not really sure, honestly. I haven't... I haven't really paid attention to exactly how close I have to be for it to start. I just know that when I have to go over to that part of the building, I start feeling on edge. So I don't think it's just being right up against the glass, it's just... that whole general area.

If you were to stand in that area, would you say the feeling is more of a fear that something bad might happen through the glass, or is it just an overwhelming, unexplained urge to avoid that specific space?

I guess... I don't really know for sure. I don't remember having a specific thought about something bad coming through the glass or anything like that. It's really just... a really strong feeling that I shouldn't be there. Like my brain is just telling me to turn around and get away from that spot. I haven't really stood there long enough to figure out exactly why it happens, I just know I need to avoid it.

When you feel that urge to get away from that area, do you find yourself needing to perform any specific actions, like counting, touching things a certain number of times, or repeating specific thoughts in your head to make the feeling go away?

No, I don't do anything like that. I don't count or have to touch things or anything. I just... I just walk away. Once I'm away from that area, the feeling kind of settles down on its own. I don't need to do any special routines to make it stop.
If you were to see a similar window in a completely different building, like a store or a friend's house, would you feel that same urge to stay away from it?

I haven't really noticed it anywhere else. Like, if I'm at the mall or at a friend's place and they have big windows, it doesn't bother me. It really just seems to be that one spot at work. I don't feel that same panic or need to get away when I see windows in other buildings.
Is there anything about that specific area at your work, such as a particular memory, event, or incident, that makes you feel like you need to avoid it?

Yeah, there is. Um... this has all been going on for about two weeks now. It started ever since a car crashed right through the store window during my overnight shift. That's the exact spot where it happened.
